reviews.title: Works sometimes
reviews.text:
This alarm is okay but the thing that infuriates me is that it will drain all of your battery within an hour. I don’t always put my phone on charge throughout the night as it damages the battery and I thought 100% would last throughout the night but Alarmy drains all my battery in an hour and a half meaning my phone dies and my alarm will not go off. This seems 
really unnecessary

reviews.text: Great alarm concept. I've used this app for five years. However, in the last few weeks, this app has been absolutely draining my battery making it a terrible experience. Please fix.

reviews.title: lol
reviews.text: I’d like to be able to choose the image/thing that I need to scan instead of a hunt, something that I actually have to get up & do in the mornings anyway, like the back door to let my dogs out. I really wasn’t a fan of the random item scan but figured it probably wakes you up more. Then this morning, the item I needed to scan was a pillow…. I didn’t even need to get out of bed to scan it, which is the whole point of the app. It also gives you the option to watch an ad for more snooze time after already giving you 3, 5 minute snoozes. This app doesn’t care about helping you get out of bed in the morning.

reviews.title: Drains battery

It feels like I’m not only seeing mire ads, but also being shoved useless features that don’t belong in an alarm app. Who ever is in charge of that, needs to be fired for sheer negligence. The feeling of having to navigate closing a mobile ad in the middle of the night to close a very loud alarm is deplorable and extremely bad UX. Y’all have so much unnecessary stuff in this app, stop it, get help

reviews.title: Good in theory - not the best in execution
reviews.text:
It works, I’ve managed to wake up with it. The choice of things to do is good 
Issue it, it’s a complete battery drain which renders it useless if it kills your phone in the night.

And even then, if you don’t have time to charge your phone form it’s dying state when you wake up, you’re screwed. 

Would be genuinely perfect if it didn’t drain my phone so bad, 20% I can deal with, but when I wake up and I’m on 0-30% it’s an issue and isn’t worth the risk.

reviews.title: Reliable alarms but awful battery usage.
reviews.text: I downloaded this app a couple of months ago to combat the awful Apple alarms that never seem to go off. It worked a treat and helps me wake up on time every single day and it also has a medication/habit alarm that goes off every night and has been amazing for keeping me on track with my meds. HOWEVER, recently I noticed that my phone kept dying in the middle of the night despite it being on around 80% battery before I went to sleep. It happened frequently enough that I checked my battery usage in my settings and was surprised to see that the app is using up to 50% of my battery every charge when my phone isn’t even on nor is the app even open. I’ve had to delete it for this reason. So just watch out for that, the premise of the alarms becomes absolutely useless when your phone dies before the alarm even gets a chance to go off…

reviews.title: Great alarm, negative user experience
reviews.text: Used the all for a while now, good for people that struggle waking up, but recently the excessive amount of ads that keep getting plastered on the screen is irritating. Especially if you have a few alarms set it’s straight after you turn off the alarm there’s an ad and if you press it just wrong while trying to get off it it will redirect you straight to safari it’s aggravating first thing you wake up to, and if you don’t swipe the app it’s a battery drainer these were never issues when I first started using the app, ads were in the low weren’t a problem at all and the background battery consumption weren’t a problem at all although the alarm itself does a fantastic job in what’s intended to do but it’s the small things that create a negative user experience.
